decision: Keep the retired engineering operation out of the new Control MCP. Retain the legacy plugin and tests until general Hermes subagent parity; preserve shared provider, approval, Docker, and environment owners.

disposition_definitions.KEEP: Preserve this file and its generic or security-critical responsibility.
disposition_definitions.RETIRE_ENTRY: Keep a named entry absent and rejected on the new MCP; this does not authorize deleting source files.
disposition_definitions.REPLACE_AFTER_PARITY: Retire or replace only after listed consumer/test paths have equivalent general Hermes ownership and verified behaviour.
disposition_definitions.SHARED_RETAIN: Keep reusable behaviour now; migrate old-role fixtures or consumers selectively after parity.

retired_entrypoints.current_state: Not registered; the capability is false and MCP call is rejected.

retired_entrypoints.name: legacy plugin engineering_run and /engineer
retired_entrypoints.current_state: Separate opt-in Hermes plugin surface; not the new generic MCP task API.
retired_entrypoints.gate: Replace only after tokenless parent-owned Hermes subagent parity and migrated consumers pass.

consumers: Control MCP tool registration
HostControlService capability projection and explicit unsupported start operation
mcp_entry_gate.parity_gate: Permanent negative contract for the new Control MCP.

consumers: Existing host lifespan, resource-only authentication, request context, protocol validation
mcp_auth_host.parity_gate: Keep the existing host/auth owner; add no parallel auth or approval store.

consumers: Control MCP observations read plugin-data/implementation_router receipts.
observations.py imports digest/source helpers from plugins/implementation_router/workspace.py.
Historical evidence is read-only and does not authorize a new run.
legacy_receipts.parity_gate: Move receipt digest/source readers to a neutral owner before retiring their current modules.

consumers: Journal/coordinator retain the old start_engineering_run intent.
Internal host dispatch and engineering owner tests cover the old operation.
tools/approval.py remains the Hermes human decision authority.
legacy_operation.parity_gate: Replace with bounded general Hermes intents after parent-owned subagent and real host approval parity.

consumers: Opt-in plugin registration and /engineer command.
Fixed actors -> ImplementationRouter -> NativeEngineeringHost workflow.
Old host consumes downstream kernel/routes/security and shared provider/environment helpers.
legacy_router.parity_gate: Retire only after existing Hermes delegation, exact-once host approval, targeted cancel/recovery and worker/child/grandchild credential isolation pass on native Windows.

consumers: Profile-scoped auxiliary model picker and Desktop locale catalogues containing generic and fixed-role copy.
legacy_ui.parity_gate: Migrate fixed-role fixtures/copy selectively; retain generic dynamic slots and locale key parity.

consumers: Old actor setup instructions and localized guides.
Control MCP retirement and implementation history.
legacy_docs.parity_gate: Replace old instructions after general subagent and migration docs exist; preserve Git history.

consumers: Router-specific workflows, qualification, sabotage and mutation scripts.
legacy_ci.parity_gate: Remove old-only checks only after equivalent general MCP/subagent security gates are required.

consumers: Generic Hermes plugins, auxiliary picker, strict provider routing and parent-owned inference.
shared_provider.parity_gate: Retain generic provider/profile routing and effort provenance; add no second credential/model store.

consumers: Generic native/Docker tools and legacy Router imports.
CI helper filters environment variables but does not isolate handles, filesystem or network.
shared_environment.parity_gate: Keep generic helpers and Docker behaviour; environment filtering is not OS-level subagent isolation proof.

consumers: mcp_serve.py remains a separate legacy stdio bridge.
permissions_respond ACK is not Hermes human approval and is never mounted on new HTTP MCP.
legacy_stdio.parity_gate: Keep separate; never reinterpret a bridge ACK as authorization.

consumers: Python package metadata, package-data entries and frozen uv dependency graph.
tests: uv lock --check after a future lock edit
packaging.parity_gate: No T02 dependency edits; remove only audited Router-only metadata after parity and review lock diffs.

consumers: Central required checks unrelated to the old Router.
Historical carry-surface artifact generated from an earlier tree.
tests: Final required checks at exact integration HEAD
central_ci_history.parity_gate: Keep central CI; regenerate carry-surface artifacts only with the native generator after source changes.

existing_no_resurrection_gate.baseline: Passed on unmodified task base. Real MCP SDK test checks tool absence, false write/start capability with an inert coordinator injected, and rejection of the retired tool call.
existing_no_resurrection_gate.tdd_note: No duplicate assertion or code edit was made because this behavioral regression already exists and passes on the task base. T02 records inventory/evidence only and claims no new RED/GREEN implementation cycle.

parity_before_source_retirement: Use existing Hermes delegation and parent provider authority; add no second harness or credential store.
Prove MCP/LLM/Git credentials, credential files, authenticated clients, inherited handles and SSH sockets are absent from worker/child/grandchild on native Windows.
Use the existing exact-once Hermes approval owner, reject MCP self-approval, and verify targeted cancellation and recovery.
Read state and verification evidence from real producers; keep prior records as labelled read-only history until their final reader is migrated.
Preserve the current Docker boundary and fail-closed engineering behaviour without requiring Docker for observation-only MCP reads.
Migrate fixed-role UI fixtures, localized strings, docs, package data, tests and old-only CI gates without removing unrelated checks.
t02_changes: No Router source deletion, workflow removal, dependency edit, endpoint activation, or client grant.
